identity.name: L-cysteine (and L-cysteine hydrochloride forms)
identity.chemical_class: Sulfur-containing amino acid and hydrochloride derivatives used as flour-treatment/dough-conditioning additives

function.mechanism: Used in dough processing; in US CFR it is defined for dough-strengthener use in yeast-leavened baked goods and baking mixes under specified limits.

adi.basis: EU additive details for E920 report ADI as 'not specified'.

efsa.key_finding: E920 remains authorised in the EU additive database; OpenEFSA file EFSA-Q-2011-00710 shows re-evaluation is still ongoing (comment updated 2026-01-19; delayed, new data call planned 2026-2027).

fda.notes: Use is limited to supplying up to 0.009 part total L-cysteine per 100 parts of flour in dough, for yeast-leavened baked goods and baking mixes.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA L-CYSTEINE entry expresses a non-numeric conclusion: 'No safety concern at current levels of intake when used as a flavouring agent'.

concerns.summary: Recent EFSA FEEDAP assessments report user-handling hazards for hydrochloride forms (eye/respiratory corrosivity/irritancy), indicating concentrated-form occupational risk rather than clear dietary consumer risk at authorised use levels.
EU food-additive re-evaluation file remains ongoing, creating uncertainty on updated modern exposure reassessment timelines.

no_concern_confirmed: E920 is still authorised in EU additive records with ADI listed as not specified.
FDA GRAS-affirmed CFR sections 184.1271/184.1272 maintain specific, narrow bakery-use conditions.
No IARC carcinogenic group classification entry was found for E920/L-cysteine in searched IARC classification lists.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric ADI is provided in the EU entry (ADI not specified), so standard ADI exceedance quantification is not directly applicable from that dataset.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory status is broadly permissive with explicit use constraints and no strong consumer-harm signal at authorised food-use levels in the sources reviewed. Uncertainty remains because EFSA re-evaluation is still ongoing and concentrated hydrochloride forms show handling hazards.
key_factors: EU authorised status with ADI listed as not specified
US CFR GRAS status with explicit low bakery-use limit
Ongoing EFSA re-evaluation and occupational handling concerns for concentrated hydrochloride forms
